anchor: free or bond
interpretation: Status does not exempt a person from this recruitment clause.

anchor: retain no more than be necessary for them
interpretation: Preference for lords is expressly limited; necessity is not numerically defined.

anchor: surety to serve
interpretation: The stated custodial endpoint requires a service commitment.

anchor: without reasonable cause or license
interpretation: Cause and licence qualify early departure; their adjudication is not specified here.

anchor: presume to receive or to retain
interpretation: The receiving employer is also exposed to a penalty.

anchor: nor that any in other manner shall demand or receive the same
interpretation: Recruitment, departure and wage limits have different objects.

anchor: all other artificers and workmen
interpretation: The craft exclusion in recruitment is not a blanket exclusion from wage regulation.

anchor: under the color of pity or alms
interpretation: Almsgivers are addressed as a way of compelling labour.

anchor: under the pain of suspension and interdict
interpretation: The episcopal letter uses ecclesiastical sanctions for stipendiary chaplains.

anchor: a whole year, or by other usual terms
interpretation: The edition preserves a qualification to annual service.

anchor: sworn two times in the year
interpretation: Compliance is renewed by an oath before local officers.

anchor: if he may serve in the same town
interpretation: The summer mobility restriction contains a local-service condition.

anchor: and other places
interpretation: The named origins do not constitute an explicitly closed list.

anchor: and safely re-
interpretation: The saving explicitly addresses a return leg as well as outward labour.

anchor: till they have found surety
interpretation: Custody can secure future compliance; it is not a manumission formula.

locator: White and Notestein 1915, p. 153; Putnam 1908, Appendix, p. 25
anchor: by their own authority, freed them
interpretation: The commission singles out self-authorized release for privately appropriated receipts without statutory observance.

locator: White and Notestein 1915, p. 154; Putnam 1908, Appendix, p. 25
anchor: the amercements and other
interpretation: The commission expressly reserves receipts due to the crown.

locator: White and Notestein 1915, p. 156; Putnam 1908, Appendix, p. 152
anchor: took excessive wages, prices, and profits
interpretation: A presentment accuses; it is not yet a verdict.

anchor: did not come
interpretation: Four named defendants do not appear on Friday; an arrest is ordered.

anchor: had been arrested and were in custody
interpretation: Saturday custody is reported before the trial disposition.

locator: White and Notestein 1915, p. 157; Putnam 1908, Appendix, p. 154
anchor: acquitted the said John Clegh
interpretation: The jury acquits the four named defendants of the presented excesses and trespasses.

locator: White and Notestein 1915, p. 157; Putnam 1908, Appendix, p. 154
anchor: Therefore let them go quit
interpretation: Discharge follows this acquittal; a general employment exemption is not recorded.
